sections.title: From demo to production

blocks.title: Not from your PDFs
blocks.text: No guide of yours covers this, so this page was written for the site, as of October 2026. Tools and versions change quickly: check the official documentation before relying on details.

blocks: Demos are easy; reliable features are the hard part, and that's where backend experience gives you an edge.

sections.title: Evaluation: how you know it works
blocks: You can't assert exact text, so you build an **evaluation set**: real questions with expected facts, and score each change against it. Without one, a prompt or model change is a guess.

blocks.title: Evaluation loop
blocks.code:
flowchart LR
  A[Collect real questions] --> B[Write expected facts]
  B --> C[Run the system]
  C --> D[Score: retrieval and answer]
  D --> E[Change prompt, chunks or model]
  E --> C
  D --> F[Run in CI to catch regressions]

rows: Treat all retrieved and user content as untrusted; limit what tools can do
Personal data sent to a provider or logged
Remove what isn't needed; check provider terms; control logs
Escape output as you would any untrusted input
Per-user limits, and maximum input and output tokens
blocks.caption: There is no complete fix for prompt injection today, so limit the damage it can do.

sections.title: Cost, latency and observability

rows: Use a smaller model where it is good enough
Saves cost and time; be careful with per-user data
Saves cost and may improve quality
Providers may offer cheaper batch processing

blocks: Log per request: model, tokens, cost, latency, retrieved documents and user feedback. Tracing with Micrometer and OpenTelemetry works as for any other service. Pin model versions, because a provider change can alter your results.

blocks.title: Interview angle
blocks.text: **Your AI feature's quality dropped after a release. How do you investigate?** Compare against the evaluation set, then check what changed: prompt, model, data or retrieval. Inspect traces for failing examples, roll back the change, and add those cases to the set.

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
- No evaluation set means no way to know.
- Assume injection is possible, and limit the blast radius.
- Track cost and tokens per feature.
- Version your prompts and pin your models.

items.question: How do you test an LLM feature in CI when output varies?
items.answer: Mock the model for unit tests, and run a scored evaluation set with pass thresholds for quality.

items.question: What usually reduces cost the most?
items.answer: Using a smaller model where quality allows, then sending less context, and caching.
